original_question: For every system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, h, do the polynomial multiple ergodic averages (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) h(T^{3n} x) and (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(T^{n^2} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1.3, Problem 11: the two specific open pointwise-convergence cases for polynomial multiple ergodic averages of powers of a single transformation.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly asks about pointwise almost-everywhere convergence, stays in the setting of a single transformation T, and identifies the exact two model averages singled out in the paper: the trilinear linear-pattern average with iterates n, 2n, 3n, and the bilinear polynomial average with iterates n and n^2.
missing_details: The paper's ambient object is an invertible measure-preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T), with 'system' defined in Section 1.2.
The functions are taken in L∞(μ), i.e. bounded measurable functions; for the second average only f and g are quantified over.
The convergence in question is as N → ∞ for the Cesàro averages (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N.
Pointwise almost everywhere should be stated explicitly as convergence for μ-almost every x ∈ X.
These are two special open cases inside the polynomial-iterate setting for powers of a single transformation; the question should not be broadened to arbitrary polynomial multiple averages.
The problem is not about commuting transformations; that is treated separately later in the paper.
refined_question: Let (X, 𝓧, μ, T) be an invertible measure-preserving system. Is it true that, for every f, g, h ∈ L∞(μ), the averages A_N(x) := (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) h(T^{3n} x) converge as N → ∞ for μ-almost every x, and that, for every f, g ∈ L∞(μ), the averages B_N(x) := (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(T^{n^2} x) also converge as N → ∞ for μ-almost every x?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5.1.3 rather than any broader neighboring problem. In that subsection, Frantzikinakis states that pointwise convergence for polynomial multiple ergodic averages is largely open and then isolates exactly two particular open cases in Problem 11. The surrounding setup in Section 5.1 shows that the discussion is about powers of a single transformation and uses the general polynomial-average template (16) with L∞ functions, while Section 1.2 provides the paper's notion of 'system'. The theorem immediately before these open problems records that mean convergence is already known for arbitrary integer polynomials, so the sharp paper-faithful reformulation should focus only on the unresolved pointwise issue for these two displayed averages, not on a broader class.
